blocks.text: This section explains how to use technology wisely and protect personal information while working online. Students learn the importance of safe habits, like using strong passwords, keeping software updated, and avoiding unsafe websites (as shown in Figure 9.2). Practicing responsible digital behavior helps prevent data loss, hacking, and identity theft. By following safety rules, users can enjoy the benefits of technology without unnecessary risks. These habits build trust and create a secure digital environment for everyone.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: A strong password with 12 characters can take millions of years for a computer to crack, but a weak one can be cracked in seconds.
Importance of Online Safety

Online safety means protecting yourself and your information while using the internet. It includes being careful about what you share, where you click, and how you store your data. Students learn that online actions leave digital footprints that can be tracked. By understanding the importance of safety, users can avoid scams, viruses, and cyber threats. Staying alert and cautious online helps keep both personal and school_related data secure.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Understanding threats and preventive measures, reduces the chance of cybercrime.
Understanding Strong Passwords and Their Role in Data Protection

A strong password is a combination of letters, numbers, and symbols that helps protect your accounts from hackers. Using unique passwords for different accounts reduces the chance of being hacked. It's best to avoid personal details like names or birthdays. Passwords should be changed regularly and not shared with others. A secure password acts as the first line of defense in protecting important files and data online.
Risks of Downloading Suspicious Software and Unsafe Browsing Habits

Downloading programs or files from unknown websites can harm your computer or steal your information. Some downloads hide viruses or spyware that collect data without permission. Unsafe browsing, such as visiting fake websites or clicking unknown links, can also lead to scams or identity theft. It is important to check sources before downloading and use antivirus tools for extra protection. Safe browsing habits help keep both devices and data secure.
Software Maintenance and Updates

Software maintenance means keeping programs and applications in good working condition by updating them regularly. Updates often fix errors, improve performance, and add new features that make software safer to use. Students learn that software companies release updates to close security gaps that hackers might exploit. Ignoring updates can lead to slow systems, crashes, or data theft. Regular maintenance keeps computers reliable, efficient, and protected from cyber threats.

When software is not updated, it becomes an easy target for hackers. Older versions may have security holes that allow unauthorized access to files or personal data. Outdated software can also cause compatibility issues with new systems or tools. Using such programs increases the risk of malware infections and data breaches. Regularly updating software reduces these risks and keeps your system safe and dependable.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Students compare features of updated vs outdated software and discuss how old versions can be attacked.
Privacy and Security Settings

Privacy and security settings help users control how their personal information is used and shared online. These settings are found in most apps, websites, and digital platforms. Students learn how to adjust them to protect personal data such as location, contacts, and browsing history. Managing privacy helps prevent misuse of information by unwanted sources or advertisers. Understanding and using these settings keeps online activities more private and secure. For example, on Instagram, users can make their account private so that only approved followers can see their posts. They can also turn off location sharing to protect their privacy and enable two-factor authentication for extra account security.
Reading and Managing Privacy Policies

Privacy policies explain how a website or app collects, stores, and uses your information. It is important to read them carefully before creating an account or agreeing to terms. By reviewing these policies, users can decide whether to share personal data or not. Students learn to check what kind of data is being collected and for what purpose. Managing privacy responsibly ensures that personal details are not shared without permission. A privacy policy tells users how their data is collected, used, stored, and shared. For example, when signing up for any social platform, the privacy policy explains what type of data may be collected, such as name, email address, location, browsing activity, and app usage. It may also explain whether this data is shared with advertisers or third-party services.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Regularly reviewing settings ensures protection as platforms update their features.
Customizing Privacy and Security Settings for Online Platforms

Most online platforms allow users to change their privacy and security settings based on their comfort level. These settings can control who sees your posts, who can contact you, and how data is used. Turning on features like two-factor authentication and limiting app permissions increases safety. The user should regularly review and update their settings as platforms often change their privacy rules. Customizing these options gives users more control over their digital presence and protection. For example, on WhatsApp, users can choose who can see their profile photo, such as everyone, only contacts, or nobody. They can also disable read receipts, commonly known as blue ticks, so that others cannot see whether their messages have been read.
Safe Online Collaboration

Online collaboration allows people to work together using digital tools from any location. It is important to use secure platforms and follow safety rules when sharing files or communicating online. Students learn to work responsibly in virtual groups while protecting personal and school data. Safe collaboration builds trust and ensures productive and respectful teamwork. For example, while using Google Docs for group work, students should share the document only with trusted classmates. They should also set the permission to “View only” instead of “Edit” if others only need to read the document. This helps protect the document from unwanted changes and keeps the work secure.
Identifying Secure Collaboration Platforms (e.g., Google Workspace, MS Teams)

Secure collaboration platforms such as Google Workspace and Microsoft Teams provide protected environments for group work. These platforms use features like encrypted communication and access controls to safeguard data. Students can share documents, attend meetings, and communicate safely. Choosing trusted and approved platforms helps protect information and reduces cyber risks. For example, students can use Google Workspace for school projects by sharing a project file only with selected classmates through restricted access. They can also use Google Meet for secure online classes, where only authorized participants are allowed to join. These features help students collaborate safely while protecting their schoolwork and personal information.
Practicing Digital Etiquette and Responsible Communication

Digital etiquette means communicating politely, respectfully, and clearly in online environments. It includes using appropriate language, respecting others’ opinions, and avoiding misuse of communication tools. Students should not share private information or behave disrespectfully during online interactions. Responsible communication promotes teamwork and helps maintain a positive and professional digital environment. For example, in a class group chat, students should respect others’ opinions during discussions. They should avoid sending spam messages, unrelated memes, or jokes during serious academic discussions. This helps keep the group useful, respectful, and focused on learning.
